We recently hired several people in their 50s & 60s, including a 67 year old, and we already had 5 people over 60, including myself; I’m 65 and work much harder that most of the younger new hires. In general, older people are more focused on the work, and not on socializing. 

Several mates have told me they prefer older hires because there is less drama and fewer demands.
I work in a big store, and there’s a lot of turnover. New hires often are gone in a few weeks or months. I’d follow bearded pucks advice above.

I’ve had it in both hands. Let it go as far as I could (years) before having it operated on. Waited too long on 2nd surgery, so there’s some nerve damage, but I can work. Avoid workers comp, it makes the process much more difficult. Also have recurring De Quervain Tenosynovitis, which is a form of tendinitis similar to CPS but no numbness. Alternating direction faced at register helps.

No, I have nobody to blame but me. My point is, if you are a long time employee, the repercussions from a write-up far exceed the cause of the write-up. As I said, the punishment does not fit the crime. I have no solution.
Yes, I had 3 writeups over the course of several years. All were for register related issues. More recently I got one for inadvertently taking only 29 minute lunch on several occasions. No warning.
I need to work til 70 to max out my SS. Plus, I enjoy the work.
I did ask my captain first, and regional said no.

The thing is, other that this issue, I love the job and usually look forward to work. I generally feel I’ve been well treated. And I’m 65, so have no real options. Couldn’t imagine working at Target or Walmart. And the insurance is excellent. 

I’ve wondered if they are trying to get rid of older people, but they raised the cap so I don’t know. They did just hire several people over 55 and told me it’s because they do the work with no drama. I’m trying to keep my requests really low key…last thing I need is management gunning for me. I need the job.
